etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English meeting, meting, from Old English mēting, ġemēting (“meeting, assembly, association, society”), equivalent to meet +‎ -ing. Cognate with West Frisian moeting (“meeting, encounter”), Dutch ontmoeting (“meeting, encounter”), Middle Low German mö̂tinge (“meeting”). Compare also German Low German Möte (“meeting, encounter”), Danish møde (“meeting, encounter”), Swedish möte (“meeting, encounter”), Icelandic mót (“meeting”). Related to moot.

definitions.definition: (gerund, uncountable) The act of persons or things that meet.
A gathering of persons for a purpose; an assembly.

quote.text:
In a meeting with government officials, Moon noted that China was “much more advanced” than South Korea in rain-making technologies, his spokesman said.
Audio (US):(file)

definitions.definition: (collective) The people at such a gathering.
An encounter between people, even accidental.
A place or instance of junction or intersection; a confluence.
(rustic US, dated) A religious service held by a charismatic preacher in small towns in the United States.

quote.citation: 1939, John Steinbeck, The Grapes of Wrath, page 20:
quote.text: You use ta give a good meetin'. I recollect one time you give a whole sermon walkin' around on your hands, yellin' your head off.

definitions.definition: (Quakerism) An administrative unit in the Religious Society of Friends (Quakers).

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English metynge, metinde, metand, from Old English mētende, *ġemētende, from Proto-Germanic *mōtijandz, present participle of Proto-Germanic *mōtijaną (“to meet”), equivalent to meet +‎ -ing.

definitions.definition: present participle and gerund of meet
